<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Reading the warm benchmark script and checking metadata index week caching.

Found redundant full-season scans within the same league. `get_team_points_simple` loads the entire season twice via two queries. `get_team_positions_simple` then calls it again. `get_league_week_table_simple` also reloads full season data for every single week. `get_honor_scores` avoids this by loading only week-specific data.

`get_team_averages_simple` and `get_individual_averages` each scan the full season in a single query. `get_team_vs_team_comparison_table` runs three queries plus nested loops, then fetches standings order with two more. The biggest bottleneck is `get_league_table_simple`: it loads all individual and team bonus data for the entire season, then filters to one week in Python. This happens once per week per league.

`get_league_averages_history` and `get_top_team_performances` both call `get_team_averages_simple` per season, duplicating the full-season scan when both are warmed for the same league. `get_top_individual_performances` adds another full-season scan via `get_individual_averages`, plus a basic data scan. `get_record_*` methods also scan the full season per season. The club matrix builder `_build_club_matrix_payload` calls `get_available_clubs()` on every invocation, triggering a fresh full club source dataframe scan.

`get_club_team_season_matrix` loads the full club source dataframe once, then for every team-season-league combination it calls `_league_final_position` and `_league_team_count`. Each helper performs separate adapter queries, so the same underlying data is fetched repeatedly.

Club legends endpoints (`get_club_legends` and `get_club_player_results_table`) each resolve the full club list independently. `ClubLegendsService` caches its player dataframe lazily per service instance, and the warm script already uses a single `ClubPlayerResultsService` holder. Still, both endpoints per club trigger redundant club list resolution.

The shard script forces `--sequential` on child processes, disabling parallelization within each season shard. Every season shard reloads LeagueService and data from scratch because of process isolation. The catalog subprocess also loads full data.

`warm_essential_caches` calls `get_season_league_standings` directly without cache assembly optimization, so it recomputes all leagues instead of assembling them from existing warm entries.

The division grid spawns jobs for the combined league plus each division. Each assembly reads the latest week from disk cache, which is efficient only if week-level caches already exist.

Cache hits are checked per language before building, and `_warm_one_multilang` builds once for the primary language. The season worker runs jobs sequentially within each season. The two top bottlenecks are the per-week `get_league_week_table_simple` loads and the nested loops in the club matrix helpers.

`get_team_positions_simple` chains `get_team_points_simple` inside the same league job batch, so the duplicate full-season scan is a quick win. `warm_essential_caches` only affects the initial on-start warmup, not the full warm script. The club-legends endpoints are medium risk because the player database is already preloaded.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
`get_available_clubs` scans the entire `computed_data` dataframe to iterate all team names. This repeated full scan is a clear bottleneck.

Club legends trigger two adapter queries per league per season. The club phase is the only warm phase using parallel workers; seasons warm sequentially and shards force sequential endpoint calls. This limits parallelism to the season level.

The catalog subprocess loads the full LeagueService merely to list seasons, leagues, and clubs. Division standings jobs read N league cache files from disk, but this is cheap when week caches already exist. Full rebuilds order jobs so week caches are built before standings, avoiding redundant reads.

Season warmup runs one season per process with `--sequential`, so every league endpoint inside that process executes serially. The dominant cost is therefore the sheer volume of endpoints multiplied by their individual build cost. A rough estimate puts roughly 860 endpoints per season when averaging 20 leagues, 18 weeks, and 15 seasons.

The seasons phase alone generates roughly 12,900 logical endpoints per season. Each `get_league_week_table_simple` call loads the full season dataframe and filters by week, which becomes catastrophic when multiplied across weeks and leagues. Quick wins include moving week filtering to the adapter level, caching per-season, per-league dataframe slices inside warm workers, sharing computed data across related endpoints, and batching club matrix position lookups.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Enough information has been gathered to compile the performance anti-pattern report.

`collect_club_matrix_jobs` rebuilds the club matrix payload for every club in a loop. Each rebuild calls `get_available_clubs()` again. This repeats a full dataframe scan per club instead of caching the result once per shard.

`_get_club_source_dataframe()` scans the entire computed dataframe and then iterates every team name in two columns with a Python loop. This is O(rows) per club matrix build multiplied by N clubs.

`_league_final_position` runs inside a nested loop. Worst case scales with teams times seasons times leagues per cell times two queries.

`warm_cache_shard.py` spawns a subprocess per catalog call. That reloads data but does not repeat inside the warm phase itself.

`cache_warmup.py` warms essential caches on startup. This is a league bottleneck for dev startup, though the user asked about warm phases.

The division standings grid reads four variants per league from disk. This is minor unless cache misses occur.

Shard children run sequentially because the code explicitly avoids threads to sidestep the GIL. Pandas vectorization releases the GIL, but Python loops inside the warmup do not. Process-level parallelism is therefore the main scaling mechanism.

Club-phase matrix generation uses a thread pool via `--club-workers`. That pool is still limited by the GIL.

`get_league_table_simple` in `app/services/league_service.py` dominates the seasons phase. It loads the full individual and team dataframes for every week endpoint without filtering at the query level. This triggers roughly twice the number of jobs per league compared to the meta phase. The repeated full dataframe scans likely consume over half the total wall time for a typical grid rebuild.

The club matrix phase is the slowest shard type. It scales with clubs times teams times seasons times leagues. Per-cell adapter queries inside nested loops add heavy overhead. The club matrix payload builder also repeats the full dataframe scan on every club.

The league-wide meta phase warms seven endpoints per league. Several endpoints scan the full unfiltered dataframe once per season. Others loop seasons separately. This multiplies the full dataframe scan cost across all meta shards.

The shard wrapper forces `--sequential` on child processes. Season and league-wide endpoints therefore run one-at-a-time per process. This leaves cores idle and bounds wall time by the sum of endpoint durations. Total CPU work does not increase, but throughput suffers.

Multiple league-wide endpoints independently query the same season and league data. `get_team_positions_simple` delegates to `get_team_points_simple`, and several meta endpoints such as `get_team_averages_simple`, `get_individual_averages`, and `get_team_vs_team_comparison_table` each fetch the same season records separately. This creates a moderate multiplier of roughly five to eight redundant scans per league and season across the seven base endpoints.

# League cache warm — performance report

Based on reading `scripts/warm_league_cache.py`, `scripts/warm_cache_shard.py`, `app/cache/cache_warmup.py`, and the `LeagueService` / club services they call.

---

## 1. Top bottlenecks (concrete)

### 1) Per-week standings re-scan full season data  
**Where:** `app/services/league_service.py` → `get_league_table_simple` (via `get_league_week_table_simple`)  
**Triggered by:** `scripts/warm_league_cache.py` → `_season_league_jobs` (2 jobs per week: `get_league_week_table` + `get_honor_scores`)

**Why:** For each week, `get_league_table_simple` loads **all** individual + team-bonus rows for the whole `(season, league)` via two `adapter.get_filtered_data` calls, then filters to one week in Python. Honor scores *do* filter by week at query time; week tables do not.

**Scale:** Per league/season: `7 + 2×weeks` jobs. Week-table jobs are ~2× the count of all other season jobs combined (e.g. 18 weeks → 36 week-table builds vs 7 other endpoints).

**Impact:** Likely **largest share of seasons-phase wall time** on full rebuild (often 40–60%+). Each miss repeats identical full-season scans.

**Fix class:** Larger refactor (one-pass multi-week standings per league/season, or week filter in the adapter query). Smaller partial win: in-process memo of `(season, league)` dataframes during a warm worker.

---

### 2) Club matrix: nested per-cell adapter queries + repeated club listing  
**Where:** `app/services/league_service.py` → `get_club_team_season_matrix`, `_league_final_position`, `_league_team_count`, `get_available_clubs`  
**Triggered by:** `scripts/warm_league_cache.py` → `_build_club_matrix_payload` / `collect_club_matrix_jobs`

**Why:**
- Every matrix build calls `get_available_clubs()` → `_get_club_source_dataframe()` (full `computed_data=True` scan) + Python iteration over all team names.
- For each team × season cell, for **each league** in the cell, `_league_final_position` and `_league_team_count` each issue separate `get_filtered_data` calls.

**Scale:** O(clubs × teams × seasons × leagues-in-cell × 2 queries), plus O(clubs) full club-list scans.

**Impact:** Clubs phase is often the **slowest shard type** when `--warm-clubs` is on; dominates club shard wall time.

**Fix class:** Larger refactor (batch final positions / team counts for all `(season, league)` once per matrix build). **Quick win:** pass precomputed `clubs` list into `_build_club_matrix_payload` instead of re-scanning per club.

---

### 3) League-wide meta: redundant per-season scans across 7 endpoints  
**Where:** `app/services/league_service.py` → `get_league_averages_history`, `get_top_team_performances`, `get_top_individual_performances`, `get_record_*`, `get_points_to_win_history`  
**Triggered by:** `scripts/warm_league_cache.py` → `_league_wide_jobs` (7 endpoints per league)

**Why:**
- `get_league_averages_history` and `get_top_team_performances` both loop all seasons and call `get_team_averages_simple` (full season scan each).
- `get_top_individual_performances` loads **unfiltered** `get_filtered_data({})` once, then per season calls `get_individual_averages` (full season scan + `iterrows`).
- Record endpoints each loop seasons with separate filtered queries.
- `get_record_games` is an alias to individual records → **duplicate** work with `get_record_individual_games` in the same warm batch.

**Impact:** **Medium–high** per league-wide shard; ~7× season-loop work where 1 shared aggregation could serve several charts/tables.

**Fix class:** Medium refactor (shared per-(league, season) snapshot for meta warm). **Quick win:** drop redundant `get_record_games` warm job (keep `get_record_individual_games` only) if API allows.

---

### 4) Redundant scans within each league/season job bundle  
**Where:** `get_team_points_simple`, `get_team_positions_simple`, `get_team_averages_simple`, `get_individual_averages`, `get_team_vs_team_comparison_table`, `get_league_history_table_data`  
**Triggered by:** `_season_league_jobs`

**Why:** Each method independently queries the same `(league, season)` data (typically 2 queries for individual + computed). `get_team_positions_simple` calls `get_team_points_simple` again. `get_team_vs_team_comparison_table` does 3 queries plus `_teams_in_standings_order` (2 more), with O(teams²) Python nested loops.

**Impact:** **~5–8× redundant dataframe filtering** per league/season before week jobs even start.

**Fix class:** Quick–medium win (memoize `(league, season)` slices on `LeagueService` for the duration of one warm job list).

---

### 5) Shard wrapper disables intra-process parallelism  
**Where:** `scripts/warm_cache_shard.py` → `_child_extra_for_script` always adds `--sequential`  
**Effect:** Each season/meta/club shard runs endpoints **one at a time** inside the child process. Season-phase `_warm_job_list` never uses `parallel_workers` (only clubs phase can, via `--club-workers`).

**Impact:** Does not add CPU work, but **under-utilizes cores within a shard**. Wall time ≈ sum of endpoint builds per shard. Process-level `--max-parallel` is the only parallelism for seasons/meta.

**Fix class:** Quick win (optional: remove `--sequential` for I/O-heavy club-legends; limited gain for CPU-bound pandas due to GIL). Larger win is fixing #1–#3 so each shard does less work.

---

### Startup-only gap (not full warm script, but league-related)  
**Where:** `app/cache/cache_warmup.py` → `warm_essential_caches`  
**Why:** Calls `league_service.get_season_league_standings()` directly, which recomputes every league’s latest week + honor scores. The full warm script’s `_assemble_season_league_standings` reads week/honor **from disk cache** instead.

**Impact:** On-start warm is slower than it needs to be for standings; does not affect `warm_league_cache.py --rebuild` path if week caches already exist.

---

## 2. Quick wins vs larger refactors

| Bottleneck | Quick win | Larger refactor |
|---|---|---|
| Per-week standings scans | Memo `(season,league)` df in warm worker | Single-pass multi-week table builder |
| Club matrix | Pass `clubs` once; cache `_get_club_source_dataframe` per worker | Batch position/count maps for all leagues in one query |
| League-wide meta | Remove duplicate `get_record_games` job; `--standings-no-division-grid` | Shared meta aggregation layer per league |
| Same-league job bundle | Service-level request-scoped cache | Rework endpoints to share computed series |
| Shard `--sequential` | Tune `--clubs-per-shard` + `--club-workers` | Allow controlled parallelism for I/O-bound steps |
| `cache_warmup` standings | Call assembly path or skip if week caches exist | Align startup warm with `warm_league_cache` phases |

---

## 3. Estimated impact (when obvious)

- **#1 per-week standings:** Highest leverage on full `--rebuild`. Incremental warm mostly hits disk on week tables → this matters mainly on new seasons or `--rebuild`.
- **#2 club matrix:** Dominates `--warm-clubs` / club shards; can be **minutes per shard** with many clubs.
- **#3 league-wide meta:** Scales with `seasons × leagues`; noticeable when `meta_per_league` shards one league per process (default in `warm_cache_shard.py`).
- **#4 redundant season bundle:** Multiplies cost of every league×season miss by ~5–8× for the non-week endpoints.
- **#5 sequential shards:** Up to **~N× longer per shard** vs theoretical parallel endpoint builds (N = viable worker count), given current CPU-bound pandas work.

---

## 4. What is already well-structured

- **Single data load per process** via `get_shared_pandas_adapter` / shared pandas store.
- **Metadata index** for `get_weeks` (`weeks_by_season_league`) — planning phase uses `week_cache` to avoid repeat lookups.
- **Multilang warm:** `_warm_one_multilang` builds once, localizes for secondary languages.
- **Standings assembly:** `_assemble_season_league_standings` reads `get_league_week_table` + `get_honor_scores` from disk when possible (avoids recomputing latest week per league).
- **Job ordering:** Week jobs before `get_season_league_standings` in `collect_jobs_for_season`.
- **Process sharding:** `build_warm_shards` splits by season / meta-league / club slices; `--skip-club-shared` on club shard 2+.
- **Club-legends:** `_warm_club_legends_worker` preloads player adapter; `ClubPlayerResultsService` holder is singleton per worker.
- **Hit/miss logic:** Per-endpoint `league_cache_try_get` with granular revision is sound; not a bottleneck compared to build paths above.
- **Benchmark tooling:** `--benchmark` / `WarmBenchmark` for identifying slow endpoints empirically.

---

## Hit/miss vs real bottlenecks

Hit/miss and i18n localize/cache I/O are **fine**. The cost is almost entirely in **miss builds**: repeated `get_filtered_data` over the same `(season, league)` slices, amplified by **per-week job multiplication** and **club-matrix nested queries**. Process sharding helps wall time but **each shard still repeats the same anti-patterns internally** because child processes always run `--sequential`.
